items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: NBC News interview (recorded Friday June 5 after the May jobs report, aired Sunday June 7), ahead of Warsh's first FOMC meeting
items.quote: We should actually lower interest rates.
items.summary: With markets pricing a hike after a strong May jobs report, Trump said 'There’s no reason to raise interest rates', called raising the benchmark rate 'the wrong thing to do' and said rates should be lowered. He said 'I’m living with Kevin' and that a country doing well should not be penalized by immediate rate increases, citing the debt.
items.score_note: Explicit call for lower rates and against any hike, ten days before the June FOMC. Date is the air date; the words were recorded on June 5.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Remarks to reporters in France after Warsh's first FOMC meeting held rates
items.quote: But we have a very good guy over there right now so I'm guided by what he wants.
items.summary: Asked about the June hold, Trump said 'It's all right. Whatever.' On the possibility of a hike he said 'It could happen', called it hard to believe and said it 'just keeps the country down', but added he is guided by what Warsh wants.
items.score_note: Dislikes the idea of a hike but defers to Warsh and makes no demand for cuts; between 0 and -1, kept at -1 because he says a hike keeps the country down.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Economic Club of New York America 250 gala dinner, Q&A after speech
items.quote: I am confident that the Fed chair will optimise the path for both inflation and economic growth
items.summary: In Q&A Bessent expressed confidence in Warsh, said Trump has complete confidence in the Fed chair to do the right thing, and predicted gas prices and inflation will come back to target now that the Iran conflict is ending. He did not call for a rate move.
items.score_note: Defers to Warsh and gives no direction for rates; the inflation-will-fall view is a mild dovish undertone but not a call.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk Box interview with Joe Kernen
items.quote: we do need to have an open mind on the price or the inflation impact of the Iran conflict
items.summary: Bessent declined to say whether he expects cuts, urged an open mind on the inflation impact of the Iran conflict and on AI productivity being disinflationary, and said Warsh came out tough on inflation. He cited Greenspan's single early-1997 'tap on the brakes' hike within a long non-inflationary expansion, which analysts read as tolerance for one hike.
items.score_note: Refuses to comment on the path; open-mind framing leans slightly dovish while the Greenspan one-hike reference leans the other way, so 0.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: CNBC interview with Joe Kernen (aired July 2)
items.quote: Now you announce positive things, and they want to bring it down by raising interest rates, and it shouldn't be that way.
items.summary: Asked whether a weak jobs number gives Warsh room to cut, Trump said Warsh has a board that is 'a little bit hostile' and 'wants to do the wrong thing', and that Warsh 'has to do what he has to do'. He complained that good data leads the Fed to raise rates and said growth need not be inflationary.
items.score_note: Opposes hikes and blames the board, but stops short of an explicit demand for cuts in this exchange.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Remarks to reporters aboard Air Force One on the opening day of the July FOMC meeting
items.quote: We should have the lowest interest rate in the world, like it used to be 30 years ago.
items.summary: Two days before the July decision Trump said 'Rates should be lowered' and that the US should have the lowest interest rate in the world, claiming growth could run far higher. He called Warsh fantastic but said other board members are 'very political' and perhaps have bad intentions.
items.score_note: Explicit call for lower rates on the eve of an FOMC decision.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Oval Office remarks to reporters after the July FOMC hold (three hawkish dissents)
items.quote: I know he’d love to see lower interest rates, but he’s got a board, and it’s a political board, and they want to keep rates up.
items.summary: After the July hold Trump said he was not disappointed in Warsh ('No, Kevin is fantastic') and blamed a 'political board' that wants to keep rates up, adding 'we fight through rates'.
items.score_note: Signals preference for lower rates and attacks the board, but no direct demand on this occasion.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk Box interview (yen intervention, FIMA facility, Fed)
items.quote: I think we have to look and think, what does an increase in the short-term rate actually do?
items.summary: Bessent questioned what a short-rate increase would achieve, said energy-related inflation is noisy while core is 'very tame', and reminded that the FOMC must look 9-18 months ahead. He backed Warsh dropping forward guidance ('every meeting should be live'), said it would be reasonable for the Fed to consider upsizing the FIMA repo facility, and said higher rates have not slowed AI capex.
items.score_note: Does not tell the Fed what to do but openly doubts the usefulness of a hike and stresses tame core inflation.
items.ai_quote: we've seen interest rates rise and we've seen no letup in this A.I. CapEx

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Punchbowl News interview, released August 7
items.quote: It's up to him a little bit, but not completely.
items.summary: Trump said he would not criticize Warsh over rate decisions, which are 'not totally up to' the chair because 'He's got a board that's very political'. He said he wants to go back to the days when strong data meant lower rates and that the US should have the world's lowest borrowing costs.
items.score_note: Restates the wish for much lower rates but pledges not to criticize Warsh and makes no specific demand; interview date not stated, release date used.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Remarks to reporters on the day the July FOMC minutes were released
items.quote: The problem is he has a board, and it's a political board
items.summary: Trump renewed his push for lower rates, saying Warsh's problem is a 'political board' of appointees of Obama, Biden and himself who 'vote to raise interest rates', and questioned whether they do so for policy or politics. He complained that good economic numbers now make things worse for interest rates.
items.score_note: Opposes the board's hiking bias and wants lower rates, without an explicit demand for an immediate cut in the quoted remarks.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk on the Street interview with Sara Eisen, day after Treasury doubled long-end buyback sizes
items.quote: I think that the Treasury and the Fed would work together if there was any change in the balance sheet
items.summary: Bessent said the larger long-end buybacks signal that yields 'don't reflect the underlying fundamentals' and that buybacks could exceed $4 billion per issue. He said a possible Fed hike 'has nothing to do' with the buyback decision, that Treasury would coordinate with any Fed balance-sheet run-off, that core inflation is down with no second-round effects, and that heavy AI-related corporate issuance is competing for capital.
items.score_note: Declines to address the rate path; dovish inflation narrative and yield-capping intent noted but no stance on what the Fed should do, so 0 rather than -1.
items.ai_quote: It is causing a short-term competition for capital

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Oval Office remarks to reporters, first comments after Warsh's Jackson Hole speech
items.quote: I think our interest rates are too high.
items.summary: Trump said he has a lot of respect for Warsh and 'he'll do what he has to do' on possible hikes, while saying US interest rates are too high. CNN reported that in the same Monday Oval Office session he called talk of raising rates 'ridiculous' because growth does not cause inflation.
items.score_note: Says rates are too high but gives Warsh a pass on hiking; between -1 and -2, the nearer-to-zero level is used.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk on the Street interview with Sara Eisen from the G20 finance ministers meeting, Asheville
items.quote: traditionally, you don't raise until a supply shock unless you see second or third order effects
items.summary: Three days after Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, Bessent refused to speculate on a September hike but said the economy has seen a supply shock, that one does not traditionally raise rates into one absent second-round effects, and that core inflation remains very restrained. He defended the buyback increase as slowing a one-way move in yields and dismissed the idea that AI build-out financing is crowding out other borrowers.
items.score_note: Lays out the case against hiking into a supply shock without explicitly telling the Fed to hold.
items.ai_quote: we keep hearing about, oh, this AI build out, the financing for that is crowding, is creating a crowding problem

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post after the August jobs report, twelve days before the September FOMC
items.quote: LOWER THE RATE OR I’LL STOP TRADING WITH COUNTRIES WITH WHICH WE HAVE A DEFICIT
items.summary: After a strong August payrolls report raised hike odds, Trump threatened to stop trading with countries that run surpluses with the US unless the Fed lowers rates, argued a stronger country means a lower interest rate, and said the Fed Board 'with its great new leader, must get smart'.
items.score_note: Explicit ultimatum demanding a rate cut.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post about two and a half hours after the FOMC raised rates 25bp
items.quote: Interest Rates in the United States should be 1%, or less, because we are the Best Credit in the World — BY FAR
items.summary: Hours after the September hike to 3.75-4.00%, Trump posted that US rates should be 1% or less and demanded 'LOWER THE INTEREST RATES FOR THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, AND FAST!'. He tied the demand to trade deficits and did not name Warsh.
items.score_note: Explicit demand for large, fast cuts right after a hike.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Remarks to reporters on arriving in North Carolina for a campaign trip, hours after the September rate hike
items.quote: And I said you might as well vote with the board because it’s not going to matter.
items.summary: Trump said he had talked to Warsh and told him he might as well vote with the board, and called the board 'very hostile' and 'very political', saying 'They’re doing the wrong thing.' He said he still had confidence in Warsh. CNBC's account of the same remarks adds that he said the board is raising rates to make him do as badly as possible.
items.score_note: Calls the hike the wrong thing on the day it was delivered; blame is directed at the board rather than Warsh.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk Box interview with Joe Kernen, first interview after the September 16 hike
items.quote: Yeah, I'm not going to talk about whether I agree with it or not.
items.summary: Asked whether he agreed with the 25bp hike, Bessent declined to say, voiced 'great confidence' in Warsh on behalf of himself and the president, and said core inflation has been quiescent with everything in the headline number. He said long yields are highly correlated with crude and crack spreads and that 'rates should come down' once the Iran conflict ends.
items.score_note: Explicitly neutral on the hike; the quiescent-core and yields-will-fall remarks lean dovish but he gives no direction for policy.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Fox News Sunday Morning Futures interview, eleven days after the September hike
items.quote: should have an open mind
items.summary: Bessent said Fed board members and FOMC officials should have an open mind, argued that AI and deregulation-driven productivity allow strong growth without inflation as under Greenspan in the 1990s, and said core inflation has eased and the energy shock is not passing through to core. Bloomberg read the remarks as an indirect call to hold off on further hikes.
items.score_note: Indirect pushback against further hikes. The source is the English edition of a Korean paper relaying Fox/Bloomberg; only the short phrase is used as the quote because longer quotes there may be back-translations (Bloomberg-derived reports confirm the 'open mind' wording).

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Time magazine interview published October 1 (interview date not stated), with follow-up remarks the same day
items.quote: I probably would have voted against the board if I were him
items.summary: Trump said he does not blame Warsh for the September hike but would probably have voted against the board in his place. Asked later the same day he said he wants Warsh to vote the way he wants. Reuters' account of the interview adds that he called the board very hostile and political and complained that interest rates will hurt growth.
items.score_note: Says the September hike should have been opposed, i.e. treats the recent hike as a mistake.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Closing Bell: Overtime interview with Brian Sullivan, hours after the FOMC held
items.quote: So I think they should have an open mind in terms of the transitory nature of the supply shock.
items.summary: After the October hold Bessent said Warsh is 'off to a great start', called the inflation an energy supply shock and cited the ECB's 2008 hike into an oil shock as a historic policy error. He said future hikes would not necessarily be a mistake because the Fed sees the economy accelerating, and warned against slowing growth enough to cut energy demand. He called stress in AI-related junk debt not problematic.
items.score_note: Urges an open mind on a transitory supply shock and invokes the ECB 2008 error, while declining to call further hikes a mistake.
items.ai_quote: the neo-clouds are a small component of the overall ecosystem

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk Box interview (excerpts released by CNBC)
items.quote: So, you know, the Fed's supposed to look into the future, not look in the rearview mirror.
items.summary: Ten days after the midterms and with a December hike priced, Bessent warned against hiking 'too much into an energy supply shock when it's coming down', called the October inflation data noisy, and predicted a benign number next given lower gasoline, crude and diesel prices.
items.score_note: Clear pushback on further hikes, framed as 'too much' rather than a demand to hold or cut.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Remarks to reporters at a White House news briefing, first Fed comments found after the midterms
items.quote: Interest rates are too high because we have a very political Fed, and I'm not blaming the chairman, by the way
items.summary: With a December hike priced, Trump said interest rates are too high because of a 'very political Fed', explicitly not blaming Warsh. He said the Fed should lower rather than keep raising rates when the numbers are strong, that the US should have the lowest rate in the world, and that lower rates would help pay off the debt.
items.score_note: Explicit call to lower rates and stop raising them, less than three weeks before the December FOMC.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk on the Street interview with Sara Eisen
items.quote: So, I would encourage the Fed to look forward, not backwards.
items.summary: Asked whether a 50bp December hike floated by a governor would be a mistake, Bessent called that governor's shift 'peripatetic', said crude and gasoline have had some of their biggest drops in history since the election, and urged the Fed to look forward rather than at noisy headline inflation.
items.score_note: Argues against a large December hike on falling energy prices; does not call for cuts.

unverified.speaker: Donald Trump
unverified.what: Washington Examiner phone interview (exclusive): Trump said he would defer to Warsh on a possible pre-midterm hike; search snippets quote him as saying 'There should be a reduction, but I'll go with the chairman', but the article body is paywalled and the Denver Gazette syndication returns 403, so the quote could not be confirmed on an opened page.

unverified.speaker: Scott Bessent
unverified.what: American Banker reports Bessent said on Tuesday (Sept 8) that Treasury buybacks are 'not doing QE' and are not meant to influence borrowing rates; article is paywalled and shows no full direct quotation.

unverified.speaker: Donald Trump
unverified.what: Reuters (Schneider/Saphir) reported that Trump told reporters he had not spoken with Warsh about the October hold; all syndicated copies found (kfgo, wsau, whbl, wmbdradio) return 403 and no direct quote was seen.

unverified.speaker: Scott Bessent
unverified.what: Fox News Radio interview in which he reportedly again called the inflation a 'temporary energy supply shock'; only a secondary aggregator mention with a fragment, no transcript or full quote found.

coverage_notes: Sources actually opened: CNBC full transcripts on the Versant press room (Bessent Jun 24, Aug 4, Aug 20, Aug 31, Sep 21, Oct 28, Nov 20; Nov 13 excerpts; Trump Jul 2), plus wire and outlet reports with direct quotes. All 20 Bessent speeches, statements and testimony texts on treasury.gov from Jun 3 to Nov 11 (sb0521 to sb0688, including the Jun 3-4 and Sep 15 hearing statements, the Jun 23 Economic Club of New York speech text and the Oct 14 IMFC statement) were opened and keyword-scanned; none mentions the Fed, policy rates, the balance sheet or private credit, so they are not itemized. The Aug 19 buyback release (sb0607) and the FSOC readouts of Jul 15 and Sep 29 contain no Bessent quotation. Not covered: Roll Call Factba.se search pages are script-rendered and returned no transcript text; whitehouse.gov transcripts were not located; Truth Social posts were taken only as reproduced by news outlets; hearing Q&A (Jun 3-4, Sep 15) was checked only through news reports, which carried no Fed quotes. Fox interviews have no transcripts online (Sep 27 item relies on a relayed short phrase; Nov 12 Fox News Radio is in unverified). Thin spots: Bessent in July (no Fed or rates remarks found), Bessent in October before the 28th, Trump in October (only the Oct 1 Time interview; his Oct 28 reaction is unverified) and Trump Nov 1-19 (no Fed comment found; his Nov 4 CNBC remarks and Nov 22 Truth Social post on the stock slide did not mention the Fed). time_et is null throughout because no page stated a clock time for the remarks. Trump repetitions on the same day were merged except Sep 16, where the Truth Social post and the later remarks to reporters are separate items.
